doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: The state of the country and the arts
summary: Asked about America, he is depressed by a culture of bullying, notes arts cut from schools, and says the news makes him want to hide.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yeah. Okay. Somehow it trickled up to them I guess. Well I have asked you some really big questions so I’ll try a bigger one. It’s not a music question but I’m interested in what’s your thoughts about the current state of our country and what we can look forward to.

When I was a hopeful person in the 1960s I never imagined things could be as bad as they are now, that there would — I think we’re moving towards a sort of culture of bullying. And I am astounded by the vast number of Americans who believe that power is more important than democracy, and who believe any absurd fantasy sci fi conspiracy theory that tickles their fancy. It’s very, very depressing.

I read in the New York Times recently a number of quotes about the arts have never been more important than they are now. Do you — would you agree with that statement? I mean I would like to but I’m not sure.

Well I think it’s certainly true in the schools, and it’s sad the extent to which the arts in the schools are the first to go when funding for education diminishes. More broadly it’s not something that I’ve given meaningful thought to.
Okay. What makes you angry these days?

Oh I wouldn’t say that I’m an angry person ever. You’ve got to push my button pretty hard before I’m an angry person. I would say that almost everything in the news makes me an ostrich, I just want to stick my head in the sand, because it feels hopeless.
